description: VERUS_SQL_COVERAGE task S: CASE (lazy), COALESCE, NULLIF, scalar subqueries (NULL, 21000), IN / NOT IN / ANY / ALL with three-valued logic and empty sets, SELECT DISTINCT and GROUP BY by value equality, WITH. Two cases use task N's integer division.

ddl.sql:
CREATE TABLE r (k integer, v numeric(10,2), tag text, d integer NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE s (k integer, w integer, n numeric(6,3));

cases.name: case_searched
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN v > 1 THEN 'big' WHEN v IS NULL THEN 'none' ELSE 'small' END AS size FROM r
cases.note: Searched CASE: first true WHEN wins; NULL v makes v > 1 Unknown (not taken).

cases.name: case_simple_no_else
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE k WHEN 1 THEN 'one' WHEN 2 THEN 'two' END AS name FROM r
cases.note: Simple CASE is k = v per WHEN; no match (and NULL k) gives the implicit ELSE NULL.

cases.name: case_mixed_scale
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN k = 1 THEN v ELSE 0 END AS x FROM r
cases.note: Common type numeric of numeric(10,2) and int: each row keeps its own scale (1.50 vs 0); typmod dropped.

cases.name: case_lazy_avoids_error
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN d > 0 THEN d ELSE 2147483647 + d END AS x FROM r
cases.note: Lazy CASE: the int4 overflow of the ELSE branch (row-dependent, not constant-folded) is never computed for d > 0.

cases.name: case_taken_branch_error
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN d > 0 THEN 2147483647 + d ELSE 0 END AS x FROM r
cases.note: The taken branch overflows int4: 22003.

cases.name: case_lazy_avoids_division_by_zero
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN d = 0 THEN -1 ELSE 10 / d END AS x FROM r
cases.note: Lazy CASE: 10 / d (row-dependent, not constant-folded) is never computed for d = 0, so no 22012 (uses task N's integer division).

cases.name: case_division_by_zero_taken
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN d = 0 THEN 10 / d ELSE 0 END AS x FROM r
cases.note: The taken branch divides by zero: 22012.

cases.name: case_bool_result
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN k > 1 THEN true ELSE false END AS b FROM r
cases.note: Boolean CASE result; NULL k takes ELSE.

cases.name: case_in_aggregate
cases.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN tag = 'a' THEN v ELSE 0 END) AS sa, COUNT(CASE WHEN v IS NULL THEN 1 END) AS nulls FROM r
cases.note: CASE inside SUM (numeric scale 2 over mixed-scale inputs) and COUNT of a CASE with implicit NULL.

cases.name: coalesce_nullif
cases.sql: SELECT k, COALESCE(v, 0) AS v0, COALESCE(tag, NULL, 'none') AS t, NULLIF(k, 1) AS nk, NULLIF(tag, 'a') AS nt FROM r
cases.note: COALESCE: first non-NULL argument, common type; NULLIF: NULL when equal, else the first argument.

cases.name: scalar_subquery_uncorrelated
cases.sql: SELECT k, (SELECT SUM(w) FROM s) AS total FROM r
cases.note: Uncorrelated scalar subquery: one row per outer row (bigint).

cases.name: scalar_subquery_empty_is_null
cases.sql: SELECT k, (SELECT w FROM s WHERE s.k = r.k AND w > 5) AS w FROM r
cases.note: Correlated scalar subquery: one row gives its value, no row gives NULL.

cases.name: scalar_subquery_cardinality
cases.sql: SELECT k, (SELECT w FROM s WHERE s.k = r.k) AS w FROM r
cases.note: k = 1 has two matching rows in s: 21000.

cases.name: scalar_subquery_where_empty
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE v > (SELECT n FROM s WHERE w > 100)
cases.note: Empty scalar subquery is NULL, so the comparison is Unknown for every row: no rows.

cases.name: coalesce_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT k, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(w) FROM s WHERE s.k = r.k), 0) AS sw FROM r
cases.note: Correlated scalar aggregate subquery (NULL on no match) inside COALESCE.

cases.name: in_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT k, tag FROM r WHERE k IN (SELECT k FROM s)
cases.note: IN keeps the matching rows (duplicates of r stay; duplicates in s do not multiply).

cases.name: not_in_with_null
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM s)
cases.note: s.k contains NULL: NOT IN is never true.

cases.name: not_in_without_null
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM s WHERE k IS NOT NULL)
cases.note: Without NULLs: 2 and 3 qualify; a NULL k is Unknown against a non-empty set.

cases.name: not_in_empty
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE k NOT IN (SELECT k FROM s WHERE w > 100)
cases.note: NOT IN of an empty set is true for every row, NULL k included.

cases.name: in_empty
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE k IN (SELECT k FROM s WHERE w > 100)
cases.note: IN of an empty set is false.

cases.name: any_all_3vl
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN k = ANY (SELECT k FROM s) THEN 't' WHEN NOT (k = ANY (SELECT k FROM s)) THEN 'f' ELSE 'u' END AS m, CASE WHEN k < ALL (SELECT k FROM s WHERE k IS NOT NULL) THEN 't' WHEN NOT (k < ALL (SELECT k FROM s WHERE k IS NOT NULL)) THEN 'f' ELSE 'u' END AS lt_all FROM r
cases.note: Three-valued ANY / ALL through CASE: a NULL element or operand gives Unknown when no element decides.

cases.name: some_numeric_cast
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE v < SOME (SELECT w FROM s) AND v >= ALL (SELECT n FROM s WHERE n IS NOT NULL AND n < 1)
cases.note: numeric vs integer subquery column (the column side is cast); SOME = ANY; ALL.

cases.name: in_grouped_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT k FROM r WHERE k IN (SELECT k FROM s GROUP BY k HAVING COUNT(*) > 1)
cases.note: IN over a grouped subquery with HAVING (TPC-H Q18 shape).

cases.name: having_correlated_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT k, COUNT(*) AS n FROM r GROUP BY k HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s WHERE s.k = r.k)
cases.note: Correlated subquery in HAVING referencing the grouping key.

cases.name: distinct_rows
cases.sql: SELECT DISTINCT k, tag FROM r
cases.note: DISTINCT removes the duplicate row; NULLs are not distinct from each other.

cases.name: distinct_ordered
cases.sql: SELECT DISTINCT tag FROM r ORDER BY tag
cases.note: DISTINCT with ORDER BY (NULLS LAST).

cases.name: distinct_value_equality
cases.sql: SELECT DISTINCT CASE WHEN d = 0 THEN 1.0 WHEN d = 1 THEN 1.00 ELSE 1 END AS x FROM r
cases.note: 1.0, 1.00 and 1 are one value: one row; the displayed scale is a plan-dependent representative (value-only).

cases.name: group_by_value_equality
cases.sql: SELECT x, COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN d = 0 THEN 1.0 WHEN d = 1 THEN 1.00 ELSE 1 END AS x FROM r) t GROUP BY x
cases.note: GROUP BY groups numerics by value across scales (one group of 5).

cases.name: cte_twice
cases.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT k, SUM(v) AS total FROM r GROUP BY k) SELECT a.k, a.total FROM t a WHERE a.total = (SELECT SUM(total) FROM t WHERE k = 1)
cases.note: WITH query referenced twice (FROM and a scalar subquery), TPC-H Q15 shape.

cases.name: cte_chain_columns
cases.sql: WITH a (kk) AS (SELECT k FROM s WHERE w IS NOT NULL), b AS (SELECT kk FROM a WHERE kk IS NOT NULL) SELECT r.k, r.tag FROM r, b WHERE r.k = b.kk
cases.note: Column aliases and a later WITH item reading an earlier one.
